target: Deniz kenarında eski bir çeşme var, yüzyıllardır akıyor.
english: By the seaside there's an old fountain, flowing for centuries.
tip: 'yüzyıllardır' means for centuries. The -dır ending on a time span shows how long something has been going on.

english: They won't talk at home.
tip: Negative future stacks -ma then -yacak on the verb: 'konuşmayacak' means will not talk. The -ma is the negative, -yacak the future.

english: They showed us around the house.
tip: 'gezdirdiler' comes from 'gezmek' (to wander); the added -dir makes it mean show around. 'bize evi gezdirdiler' = they showed us the house.

english: You must come to the meeting on time.
tip: The -meli in 'gelmelisiniz' means must or should. Personal endings come after it: 'gelmelisiniz' = you must come.

english: The place we'll go is very far.
tip: 'gideceğimiz' describes the noun 'yer': the place we will go. Turkish puts this whole clause before the noun, with no word like which.

english: If we wake up early we'll have breakfast.
tip: 'kalkarsak' is the if form: 'kalkar' plus -sak. 'eğer' only flags the condition and can be dropped, 'kalkarsak' still means if we get up.

english: My mother told me to get up early tomorrow.
tip: To report a command, turn the verb into a noun plus possessive: 'kalkmamı söyledi' means told me to get up, literally said my getting-up.

target: Her gece yatmadan önce diş fırçalarım.
english: I brush my teeth every night before bed.
tip: 'yatmadan önce' means before going to bed: verb plus -madan önce is the before-doing pattern, and the verb stays in its base form.

target: Arkadaşım filmin çok iyi olduğunu söyledi.
english: My friend told me the film was very good.
tip: For a reported statement Turkish turns the verb into a noun: 'olduğunu söyledi' means said that it was. The inner subject 'filmin' takes the -in ending.

target: Daha dikkatli olsaydık bu kaza olmazdı.
english: If we had been more careful this accident wouldn't have happened.
tip: Unreal past condition: 'olsaydık' means if we had been, paired with 'olmazdı', would not have happened. Both look back on what did not occur.

target: Bu akşam misafir gelecek, hazırlık yapmam lazım.
english: Guests are coming tonight, I need to prepare.
tip: 'yapmam lazım' means I need to prepare: 'yapma' plus possessive -m plus 'lazım'. Swap the ending for who: 'yapman lazım' is you need to.

target: Komşumuz hafta sonu film izledi ama bitiremedi.
english: Our neighbor watched a movie on the weekend but couldn't finish.
tip: 'bitiremedi' means could not finish: the -eme inside marks inability, unlike plain 'bitirmedi', which just means did not finish.

english: I won't attend the meeting tomorrow.
tip: 'katılmak' takes the -a/-e ending: you attend to something, so it is 'toplantıya', not 'toplantıyı', before 'katılmayacağım'.

english: When it was snowing, I took my umbrella.
tip: 'yağdığında' means when it snowed: verb plus -dığında builds a when clause. 'kar yağdığında' sets the time for the main verb.

english: I had my car repaired by the mechanic.
tip: 'ettirdim' means I had it done, versus plain 'ettim' I did. The person doing the work takes the -e/-a ending: 'tamirciye', to the mechanic.

english: As the weather warmed up, I put on my raincoat.
tip: 'ısınınca' means once it warmed up: verb plus -ınca marks as soon as or when, linking the two events in time.

english: The company I work for is an international firm.
tip: 'çalıştığım' means the one I work at: -tığım turns the verb into a modifier placed before 'şirket', with no separate word like that.

target: Yıl sonuna kadar Türkçeyi iyi konuşuyor olacağım.
english: By the end of the year I will be speaking Turkish well.
tip: 'konuşuyor olacağım' means I will be speaking: present -yor plus 'olacağım' gives an ongoing future action, not a one-time will speak.

english: He/She won't do in the library.
tip: 'yapmayacak' is the negative future: the -ma marks not and -yacak marks will, so it means will not do.

english: Since you're coming, come early.
tip: 'madem geleceksin' means since you are coming. 'madem' opens a given-that reason and usually pairs with a command or plan, here 'erken gel'.

english: The work you'll do is very important.
tip: 'yapacağın iş' means the work you will do. The -acağın ending makes a future verb describe the noun 'iş' right after it, with no word like that.

english: When summer comes we will swim in the pool.
tip: 'gelince' means when it comes or once it comes. Verb plus -ince links one event to the next, so 'yaz gelince' sets the time for the main verb.

english: He/She will write in the park next week.
tip: 'parkta' means at the park. The k in 'park' is voiceless, so the ending takes -ta, not -da: 'parkta', never 'parkda'.

english: Everything you said turned out to be true.
tip: 'söylediğin' means that you said. The -diğin ending turns the verb into a modifier before 'her şey', so 'söylediğin her şey' is everything you said.

english: From tomorrow on we begin the new program.
tip: 'yarından itibaren' means from tomorrow on. 'itibaren' needs the -dan ending on the time word, giving 'yarından' from 'yarın'.

target: Saat kaç? Saat üçü çeyrek geçiyor.
english: What time is it? It's a quarter past three.
tip: 'saat üçü çeyrek geçiyor' means quarter past three. For minutes past the hour, the hour takes -ü and 'geçiyor' means is passing.

target: Bu gece sıfırın altında beş derece olacakmış.
english: It will be five degrees below zero tonight apparently.
tip: 'olacakmış' means it will be, going by what was heard. The -mış after the future -acak adds an apparently or reportedly to the prediction.

english: He painted the walls of his room blue.
tip: 'maviye boyadı' means painted it blue. With 'boyamak' the resulting color takes -e, so 'mavi' becomes 'maviye'.

english: This shovel was cleaned last summer.
tip: 'temizlendi' means it was cleaned. The -n inside 'temizlemek' flips it so the shovel is acted on rather than doing the cleaning.

english: I will study until my mother comes.
tip: 'gelene kadar' means until she comes. Verb plus -ene kadar marks until that happens, so 'annem gelene kadar' sets how long the studying lasts.
